newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares higher amid bond market recovery.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares higher amid bond market recovery.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher in mixed trading following another rise in the bond market, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.31 points, or 0.72 percent, to 184.02 on an all-share turnover of 67 million shekels against 56 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 index rose 0.43 percent to 194.09.

"The market continues to rise and looks relatively good. The market has gained almost six percent during the last 10 days mainly because of the improvement in the bond market," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investment and Securities.
"Activity is still low and the main buyers are portfolio managers who are using the opportunity to buy shares," Hoffman added.

Prices of bonds linked to the consumer price index have gained 0.9 percent in the past week while unlinked bonds rose 0.5 percent as provident funds, which were dumping bonds, have halted their sales.
Elite Industries rose 5.50 percent to 1,116 on volume of 1.9 million shekels. Traders said there was no specific reason for the rise and the company said it was not planning any announcement.
Dead Sea Bromine surged 5.5 percent to 1,531 but traders said the share rose on low turnover.
Tadiran rose 0.75 percent to 1,304 after Koor Industries reported it had raised its stake in the company in the past 10 days to 62.07 percent from 61.9 percent.
Koor, the most active share, gained 1.5 percent to 27,081 on high turnover of 7.8 million shekels.
"The session opened with nice gains but towards the end of the trading day the market started falling because of high activity of speculators in Maof index options," said one trader.
"The rise we have seen during the last week is an outcome of the improvement in the bond marekt," he said.

Africa Israel Investments, the second-most active share, rose 2.75 percent to 483,594 on volume of 2.7 million shekels. Africa's second issue, the third-most active share, surged 6.5 percent to 367,651 on turnover of 2.6 million shekels. Traders said the only buyer in Africa Israel was its parent company Bank Leumi.
